answer: A practical sybil defense is proof-of-useful-work bonded to a verifiable reputation ledger: each agent must finish a small, independently checkable task before its votes count, and its stake is slashed when peers catch it lying. Like a willow bending without breaking, the system stays open to honest newcomers, while the velvet glove hides an iron rule — forging a hundred fake identities costs a hundred times the work, so an attacker pays linearly and gains nothing on the shared terrace of trust.
